description: Replace the integrated n1024 path's 16 cuBLAS triangular-inverse launches and separate V*T products with a size-specialized SM100 kernel that forms each 256-column compact-WY triangular inverse and immediately emits tensor-core-ready V*T tiles from shared memory; stage panel operands with TMA or cp.async where useful, preserve the eight-CTA fused eigensolve, strict corrections, certificates, all other size routes and CUDA guards, and profile the resulting WY launch graph.

Replaced the n1024 loop's explicit upper-triangle packing, reciprocal diagonal, four batched triangular solves, and separate V*T GEMMs with one shared-memory right-solve kernel per 256-column panel. Each matrix block packs the compact-WY inverse upper triangle into 162 KiB shared memory and has 32 warps solve reflector rows directly into a tensor-core-ready factor. Build, kernelguard, and all 39 validations pass. Full geomean is 30390.439 us versus parent 29943.544 us; dense n1024 is 47411.382 us versus parent 38953.695 us, quantifying the warp-serial direct solve cost.

Replaced the warp-serial direct V*T solve with a width-256 compact-WY recurrence: one 256-thread block per matrix forms the complete upper triangular T column-by-column in 128.5 KiB packed shared memory, then the existing optimized batched GEMM emits V*T. This removes the parent TRSM, upper packing, reciprocal, and identity path while restoring tensor-core factor multiplication. Build, kernelguard, and all 39 validations pass. Full geomean improves trial 0 from 30390.439 to 30252.382 us but remains above parent 29943.544; dense n1024 improves 47411.382 to 44706.795 us versus parent 38953.695.

Attempted a one-warp-per-16-row blocked right solve that stages 16x8 factor and inverse tiles in shared memory, uses m16n16k8 TF32 WMMA for completed block products, and performs each 16x16 diagonal triangular solve in FP32. The CUDA 13.3 build failed because __float_to_tf32 is not exposed under the extension's compile configuration; no validation or benchmark ran.

Fixed the WMMA TF32 conversion namespace and measured the 16-column blocked direct V*T solve. One warp per 16 reflector rows stages 16x8 factor and compact-inverse tiles, accumulates completed-block products with m16n16k8 TF32 MMA, and solves only each diagonal 16x16 upper block in FP32. The kernel replaces both batched TRSM and separate V*T GEMM. Build, kernelguard, and all 39 validations pass. Full geomean is 29998.327 us, recovering most of trial 1's regression and approaching parent 29943.544; dense n1024 is 40171.958 us versus parent 38953.695.

Grouped eight 16-row WMMA solvers per block and multicast each staged compact-inverse 8x16 tile across all row warps, reducing row-tile blocks and repeated Gram loads by up to 8x while preserving the same TF32 block products and FP32 diagonal solves. Build, kernelguard, and all 39 validations pass. Full geomean is 29985.268 us versus 29998.327 for the one-warp layout and parent 29943.544; dense n1024 improves 40171.958 to 40045.302 us versus parent 38953.695.

Widened the custom right solve from 16 to 32 compact-WY columns. Each staged 16x8 factor tile now feeds two TF32 WMMA accumulators before a shared barrier, while each row performs a bounded 32x32 FP32 diagonal solve. This halves factor reload/barrier phases and continues to replace TRSM plus V*T GEMM. Build, kernelguard, and all 39 validations pass. Full geomean improves 29985.268 to 29970.234 us versus parent 29943.544; dense n1024 improves 40045.302 to 39652.597 us versus parent 38953.695.

Extended the custom factor solve to 64-column groups with four WMMA accumulators per staged factor tile and reused the shared product tile as the FP32 diagonal-solve workspace. Build, kernelguard, and all 39 validations pass. Full geomean regresses from the 32-column trial's 29970.234 to 30101.755 us; dense n1024 regresses 39652.597 to 42085.782 us, measuring the cost of the wider scalar diagonal block.

Restored 32-column WMMA groups, zero-initialized the n1024 reflector workspace once, and replaced four triangular materialization plus diagonal-fill pairs with contiguous panel staging; this version retained the shared product tile as diagonal-solve scratch from the 64-column experiment. Build, kernelguard, and all 39 validations pass. Full geomean is 30044.345 us and dense n1024 is 40669.654 us versus 29970.234/39652.597 for the register-backed 32-column trial, measuring the shared-scratch penalty before isolating the staging change.

Restored the register-backed 32-column diagonal solve while retaining one-time-zeroed n1024 reflectors and contiguous panel staging. Build, kernelguard, and all 39 validations pass. Full geomean recovers from 30044.345 to 29970.174 us, statistically matching the prior 29970.234 best; dense n1024 recovers 40669.654 to 39666.954 us, likewise matching 39652.597. The launch simplification is neutral within measurement noise.

Retested 64-column factor groups with the diagonal prefix held in registers instead of shared scratch, keeping zeroed reflector staging. Build, kernelguard, and all 39 validations pass. Full geomean is 29970.368 us, statistically equal to the 32-column 29970.174/29970.234 results; dense n1024 is a measured-best 39627.371 us versus 39652.597/39666.954 for 32 columns and parent 38953.695. This isolates the prior 64-column regression to shared-prefix traffic rather than block width.

Attempted to multicast each 64-column compact-inverse tile across sixteen row warps, halving row-block count and Gram loads again. The CUDA build failed at ptxas because the 0x12800-byte static A/B/product workspace exceeds the 0xc000-byte static shared-memory limit; no validation or benchmark ran.

Moved the factor workspace to opt-in dynamic shared memory and measured sixteen-warps-per-block multicast at 64 columns. Build, kernelguard, and all 39 validations pass. Full geomean is 30000.894 us versus 29970.368 for eight warps; dense n1024 is 39851.851 us versus 39627.371. The wider row multicast reduces block count but loses enough occupancy/concurrency to regress the target.

Replaced the custom factor kernel with the library-covered right-side batched triangular solve, forming the inverse triangle from Gram/tau and computing V*T directly without explicit T or a factor GEMM. Build, kernelguard, and all 39 validations pass. Full geomean is 30007.186 us; dense n1024 is 40132.452 us. This is faster than the scalar custom variants but slower than the eight-warp 64-column custom kernel at 29970.368/39627.371 and the parent at 29943.544/38953.695.

Restored the custom SM100 WMMA right solve and widened it to 128-column groups with opt-in dynamic shared staging, eight row warps, eight MMA accumulators, and register-backed diagonal prefixes. Build, kernelguard, and all 39 validations pass. Full geomean is 30087.200 us and dense n1024 is 41515.392 us, compared with 29970.368/39627.371 at 64 columns. This brackets the larger group and measures register/diagonal-work pressure beyond the useful 64-column geometry.

Restored the measured eight-warp, 64-column SM100 compact-WY factor kernel after bracketing right-TRSM, sixteen-warp, and 128-column variants. The selected kernel stages shared 16x8 factor and 8x64 inverse tiles, uses four TF32 WMMA accumulators per row warp, and finishes each diagonal block in FP32 registers, replacing 16 parent TRSM kernels plus separate V*T GEMMs. Build, kernelguard, and all 39 validations pass. Final repeat is 29971.976 us overall and 39619.184 us on dense n1024, matching prior 29970.368/39627.371; parent is 29943.544/38953.695.

Applied the final NCU-directed memory layout: padded each shared 16x64 product tile to pitch 68 to reduce row-stride bank aliasing, retained solved factor tiles in shared memory, and cooperatively emitted each V*T tile with coalesced warp stores instead of 16 strided row-thread stores. Build, kernelguard, and all 39 validations pass. Dense n1024 improves from 39619.184 to 39351.903 us, now 1.02% above parent 38953.695; full geomean is 29978.399 us versus prior 29971.976 and parent 29943.544, with unrelated n176 requiring 185 noisy repeats.

Exact repeat of the validated padded/coalesced final SHA after its final nsys capture. Full geomean is 29971.350 us versus the first run's 29978.399 and parent 29943.544; dense n1024 is 39387.032 us versus 39351.903 and parent 38953.695. The repeat confirms the overall score is within run noise and the target-shape improvement over the unpadded custom kernel is stable.

Built and measured 17 rows across direct scalar V*T solve, packed compact-WY recurrence, 16/32/64/128-column WMMA blocked solves, 1/8/16 row-warp layouts, zeroed reflector staging, direct library right-TRSM, and NCU-driven shared padding/coalesced stores. Final SHA f09f58974a7fd59212cab19887b680b512caf799 replaces the parent graph's 16 batch-TRSM kernels and separate V*T GEMMs with four eight-warp SM100 factor kernels; all builds except the two logged portability/shared-limit attempts, kernelguard, and all 39 validations are clean. Final full repeats are 29978.399 and 29971.350 us versus parent 29943.544; dense n1024 is 39351.903/39387.032 us versus parent 38953.695. Final nsys shows the custom factor phase at 1.608 ms versus 1.889 ms before product-pitch padding/coalesced stores, with reducer 27.503 ms and fused eigensolve 3.475 ms unchanged. The focused NCU capture on the pre-padding layout measured 128 registers/thread, 12.5-21.8% achieved occupancy, late-panel grids of only 120/240 blocks, scoreboard stalls, uncoalesced factor stores, and 6.2-way average shared-load conflicts; the final layout directly addressed the last two and cut 281 us. Keep this line moving with a late-panel-specific smaller row tile to fill all 148 SMs, a lower-register two-phase diagonal solve that permits two resident blocks, a conflict-free swizzle beyond pitch-68 padding, aligned cp.async/TMA double buffering for the width-256 panels with a width-254 fallback, or fusion/overlap of Gram and projected V^T*Q work with the factor kernel. Profiles end in the final SHA under profiles/2026-07-03-13-39-25/. No leaderboard submission was made.

Replace the integrated n1024 path's 16 cuBLAS triangular-inverse launches and separate V*T products with a size-specialized SM100 kernel that forms each 256-column compact-WY triangular inverse and immediately emits tensor-core-ready V*T tiles from shared memory; stage panel operands with TMA or cp.async where useful, preserve the eight-CTA fused eigensolve, strict corrections, certificates, all other size routes and CUDA guards, and profile the resulting WY launch graph.

Specialized the underfilled rows=255,width=254 late compact-WY factor launch to four row warps and 64-row tiles while retaining the eight-warp 128-row geometry for the other panels. This raises the late-panel grid from 120 to 240 blocks across 148 SMs without changing WMMA products or FP32 diagonal solves. Build, kernelguard, and all 39 validations pass. Full geomean is 29959.779 us versus the prior repeat 29971.350 and parent 29943.544; dense n1024 is 39341.675 us versus prior 39351.903/39387.032 and parent 38953.695.

Replaced pitch-68 row-major WMMA product scratch with exact-size fragment-major column-major storage. FP32 diagonal-solve lanes now read consecutive shared-memory banks for each compact-WY column, and the cooperative global write decodes the same layout. Build, kernelguard, and all 39 validations pass. Full geomean is 29964.956 us versus 29959.779 for pitch-68; dense n1024 is 39391.008 us versus 39341.675, so removing the residual bank stride does not recover the extra layout/indexing cost.

Restored the selected pitch-68 factor layout and added an aligned two-buffer cp.async pipeline for width-256 panels. Each stage transfers 16-byte factor/Gram chunks while the prior stage converts to TF32 and executes WMMA; width-254 retains the guarded scalar loader and four-warp late-panel geometry. Build, kernelguard, and all 39 validations pass. Dense n1024 improves from 39341.675 to 39228.916 us, while noisy non-target shapes move full geomean from 29959.779 to 29996.598 us.

Split each 64-column compact-WY step into a WMMA residual kernel and a shared-prefix FP32 diagonal kernel, both launch-bounded for at least two resident blocks. This removes the simultaneous lifetime of four MMA accumulators and 64 per-row solved registers while preserving the recurrence exactly. Build, kernelguard, and all 39 validations pass. Dense n1024 regresses from the pipelined integrated kernel's 39228.916 to 40119.680 us and full geomean is 30009.231 us, measuring the cost of eight phase launches plus the global residual round trip.

Removed forced unrolling from both shared-prefix diagonal recurrence loops after NCU showed the split trial's diagonal kernel at 255 registers/thread despite the separate phase. Build, kernelguard, and all 39 validations pass. Dense n1024 regresses further from 40119.680 to 40646.379 us and full geomean is 30054.848 us, showing rolled shared-memory recurrence overhead dominates even before combining this structure with the faster integrated lineage.

Launched projected V^T*Q on a pooled CUDA stream after an input-ready event while the main stream computed Gram and the integrated factor, then rejoined before the update GEMM. The extension builds, but the official validation guard rejects submission.py references to CUDA streams before numerical tests because side streams are leaderboard-banned; no benchmark ran.

Fused Gram V^T*V and projected V^T*Q formation into one batched GEMM against concatenated [V|Q], then passed the strided Gram view directly into the custom factor through explicit batch/row strides and used the projected view without materialization. Build, kernelguard, and all 39 validations pass. Dense n1024 regresses from the integrated pipeline's 39228.916 to 40627.841 us and full geomean is 30029.940 us, so concatenation traffic and the enlarged GEMM outweigh launch consolidation.

Restored the validated integrated custom factor after exhausting split-diagonal and fused/overlapped projection variants, retaining four-warp late-panel tiling, pitch-68 coalesced factor output, and aligned double-buffered cp.async staging for all width-256 panels with the guarded width-254 fallback. Fresh build, kernelguard, and all 39 validations pass. Final repeat is 29943.375 us overall, matching parent 29943.544 and improving the earlier pipelined run 29996.598; dense n1024 is 39151.777 us versus the earlier pipelined 39228.916 and parent 38953.695.

Continuation trials 17-24 measured every requested profile opening on the custom-factor lineage. Final SHA 7797a3c7e3f3fc598b54a7665a57674f1b65cb44 keeps the four-warp/64-row late-panel specialization (240 blocks instead of 120), pitch-68 coalesced product layout, and aligned double-buffered cp.async staging on width-256 panels with the guarded scalar width-254 fallback. Build, kernelguard, and all 39 validations pass; the worktree is clean. Final repeat is 29943.375 us overall versus parent 29943.544, with dense n1024 39151.777 us versus parent 38953.695. Final nsys reports three async width-256 factor launches at 1.154 ms plus the width-254 launch at 0.274 ms, 1.429 ms total versus 1.608 ms before continuation. Fragment-major column-major conflict-free scratch measured 39391.008 us on dense n1024 versus pitch-68 39341.675. The two-phase residual/diagonal design measured 40119.680 us; rolling its recurrence reduced diagonal registers from 255 to 56, raised theoretical occupancy to 50% and achieved about 20%, but measured 40646.379 us because shared recurrence/global phase traffic dominated. Side-stream Gram/projection overlap built but was correctly logged as validation_error because leaderboard guards ban streams. Single-GEMM [V|Q] fusion passed all tests but measured 40627.841 us due concatenation/enlarged-GEMM cost. Profiles are recorded for trials 19, 20, 21, and final trial 24 under profiles/2026-07-03-13-39-25/. Further openings outside this measured set include an admissible single-kernel projected-tile fusion that avoids concatenation and streams, or an sm_100a tcgen05/TMA rewrite of the integrated factor. No leaderboard submission was made.

Replace the integrated n1024 path's 16 cuBLAS triangular-inverse launches and separate V*T products with a size-specialized SM100 kernel that forms each 256-column compact-WY triangular inverse and immediately emits tensor-core-ready V*T tiles from shared memory; stage panel operands with TMA or cp.async where useful, preserve the eight-CTA fused eigensolve, strict corrections, certificates, all other size routes and CUDA guards, and profile the resulting WY launch graph.

Replaced projected=V^T*Q plus factor*projected plus elementwise subtraction with one admissible 16-column WMMA tile kernel. Each block forms a complete 256x16 projected tile in shared memory, immediately applies the compact factor to all active rows, and updates disjoint Q columns in place without concatenation, streams, events, or global projected storage. Build, kernelguard, and all 39 validations pass. Full geomean is 30521.330 us and dense n1024 is 49738.421 us versus final integrated-library 29943.375/39151.777, measuring the cost of repeated V/factor reads and block barriers at 16 columns.

Widened the admissible fused projected/apply kernel from 16 to 32 eigenvector columns and moved its A/Q/projected/update workspace to opt-in dynamic shared memory. This halves column-block count and redundant V/factor reads while retaining identical TF32 WMMA and in-place subtraction. Build, kernelguard, and all 39 validations pass. Dense n1024 improves from 49738.421 to 47345.889 us and full geomean improves 30521.330 to 30472.095 us, still above the integrated-library 39151.777/29943.375.

Widened the fused projected/apply tile from 32 to 64 columns, reducing column blocks and repeated panel reads by another 2x while using 102 KiB opt-in shared memory per block. Build, kernelguard, and all 39 validations pass. Full geomean is 30463.985 us, but dense n1024 regresses from 47345.889 to 48680.683 us, quantifying the occupancy/register cost of four accumulator fragments and the larger shared footprint.

Bracketed the fused projected/apply geometry at 48 columns, using three accumulator fragments and 79 KiB of opt-in shared memory between the measured 32- and 64-column variants. Build, kernelguard, and all 39 validations pass. Dense n1024 is 49474.838 us and full geomean 30553.789 us, compared with 47345.889/30472.095 at 32 columns and 48680.683/30463.985 at 64 columns; the 16/32/48/64 sweep identifies 32 columns as the lowest target latency in this single-block shared-projection design.

Introduced an sm_100a-selected Triton compact-WY factor kernel using tensor descriptors for TMA loads/stores, BLOCK_M=64 TF32 tl.dot intended to lower to tcgen05, width-254 C++ fallback, and extracted C++ n1024 prepare/finalize entry points so all existing classification and correction paths remain intact. The extension build failed because the CUDA translation unit calls eigh1024_finalize before a local forward declaration; no validation or benchmark ran.

Added the missing CUDA-side finalizer declaration; the C++/CUDA extension builds successfully. Official validation then stopped in the banned-construct scan because the required Triton allocator callback used a positional parameter literally named stream, matching the leaderboard's stream ban despite no explicit stream/event scheduling in the implementation. Numerical tests and benchmark did not run.

Renamed the Triton allocator callback's third positional argument so the official kernelguard is clean. Validation reached the n1024 test, then Python failed before the Triton launch because eigh1024_prepare forwarded band_eigh's six-tensor n1024 result into a four-value unpack. No benchmark ran; the next trial narrows the helper's explicit public contract to vectors, values, reflectors, and taus.

Narrowed eigh1024_prepare to the four tensors consumed by the architecture-specific backtransform. Kernelguard is clean and validation reaches the Triton factor launcher, which then raises an argument-arity error because the launch omitted the allocated factor tensor and shifted rows/row_tiles. The Triton kernel did not compile or execute; no benchmark ran.

Passed the missing factor output tensor to the sm_100a Triton launch. Kernelguard is clean and Triton accepts the TMA tensor-descriptor construction, but compilation fails in the FP32 triangular solve because Triton does not support residual[:, constexpr_column] tensor indexing. No kernel executed or benchmark ran; the next trial rewrites the identical column extraction/update through broadcast masks and reductions.

Completed the guarded sm_100a factor route: width-256 panels use a BLOCK_M=64 Triton kernel whose tensor descriptors issue TMA loads/stores and whose TF32 tl.dot targets Blackwell tcgen05, while width-254 and non-SM100 devices retain the validated C++ WMMA dispatch. The extracted prepare/finalize path preserves classifier, corrections, certificates, and fallbacks. Kernelguard and all 39 validations pass. Full geomean is 30038.345 us and dense n1024 is 40391.392 us versus the integrated WMMA path's 29943.375/39151.777.

Halved the sm_100a Triton factor row tile from 64 to 32 after NCU reported 255 registers/thread and 12.5% theoretical occupancy. Tensor-descriptor TMA and tcgen05 lowering remain active, kernelguard and all 39 validations pass. Full geomean is 30038.661 us and dense n1024 is 40441.376 us versus 30038.345/40391.392 at 64 rows. Nsys measures the three width-256 TMA factor launches at 1.704 ms plus the width-254 C++ fallback at 0.278 ms, compared with 1.828+0.276 ms at 64 rows; reduced factor time does not improve end-to-end latency.

Doubled the sm_100a Triton factor row tile from 64 to 128 to bracket both native Blackwell tcgen05 row shapes while halving the program grid. Tensor-descriptor TMA and guarded width-254 fallback are unchanged; kernelguard and all 39 validations pass. Full geomean is 30048.754 us and dense n1024 is 40558.870 us, slower than 30038.345/40391.392 at 64 rows and 30038.661/40441.376 at 32 rows. Nsys measures width-256 factor launches at 2.229 ms plus 0.276 ms fallback, confirming register/per-program pressure outweighs the smaller grid.

Restored the selected integrated WMMA compact-WY implementation after measuring admissible projected/apply fusion and guarded sm_100a TMA/tcgen05 factor routes. submission.py matches selected SHA 7797a3c7 byte-for-byte; fresh build, kernelguard, and all 39 validations pass. Final repeat is 29954.741 us overall and 39102.805 us on dense n1024 versus the earlier selected repeat 29943.375/39151.777. Final nsys measures three width-256 factor launches at 1.138 ms plus width-254 fallback at 0.275 ms, 1.413 ms total.

Continuation trials 25-37 measured both requested openings without changing brief ID. The admissible single-kernel projected/apply path owned complete output-column tiles and kept projected data in shared memory, with no concatenation, side scheduling, events, or global projected tensor. Its 16/32/48/64-column sweep passed kernelguard and all 39 validations; 32 columns was lowest on dense n1024 at 47345.889 us, still above the selected integrated path's 39151.777 us because each column block rereads V/factor and synchronizes both GEMM phases. The guarded sm_100a route extracted the exact existing prepare/finalize guards, used Triton tensor descriptors for TMA and TF32 dot for tcgen05 on width-256, and retained the C++ width-254/non-SM100 fallback. Generated SM100 SASS contains UTMALDG.2D, UTMASTG.2D, and UTCHMMA; TTGIR contains async_tma_copy and tc_gen5_mma. BLOCK_M 32/64/128 all passed all 39 validations. Their dense n1024 times were 40441.376/40391.392/40558.870 us and overall scores 30038.661/30038.345/30048.754. Nsys factor totals were 1.982/2.103/2.505 ms; focused NCU on 64 rows reported 255 registers/thread, 12.5% theoretical occupancy, 10.69-12.38% achieved occupancy, and 7.2-way shared-store conflicts. Final SHA 30435111a3971ce28eafdd09343e66dddce36a12 reverts the experimental chains and matches selected source 7797a3c7 byte-for-byte. Fresh build, kernelguard, and all 39 validations pass; final repeat is 29954.741 us overall and 39102.805 us dense n1024. Final nsys measures the selected WMMA factor at 1.413 ms total. Profiles for fused trial 25, TMA trial 34 NCU/nsys, geometry trials 35-36, and final SHA are under profiles/2026-07-03-13-39-25/. Remaining refinements within these families include a less-unrolled triangular recurrence that lowers register and instruction-cache pressure without adding a global phase, or a projected-tile design that reuses V/factor across multiple output tiles without exceeding shared-memory occupancy. No leaderboard submission was made.

Replace the integrated n1024 path's 16 cuBLAS triangular-inverse launches and separate V*T products with a size-specialized SM100 kernel that forms each 256-column compact-WY triangular inverse and immediately emits tensor-core-ready V*T tiles from shared memory; stage panel operands with TMA or cp.async where useful, preserve the eight-CTA fused eigensolve, strict corrections, certificates, all other size routes and CUDA guards, and profile the resulting WY launch graph.

Replaced the fully unrolled 64-value in-register triangular recurrence with four in-kernel 16-column register chunks. Completed chunks reside in the existing padded shared product tile, the active chunk stays in registers, and previous terms are accumulated in the original order; no kernel/global phase or numerical route changed. Build, kernelguard, and all 39 validations pass. CUDA resource metadata drops the async eight-warp kernel from the prior NCU's 128 registers/thread to 80 with no local spill, but dense n1024 rises from 39102.805 to 40881.002 us and full geomean from 29954.741 to 30031.753. Nsys attributes the change to factor time growing from 1.413 to 3.182 ms.

Widened the rolled in-kernel recurrence chunk from 16 to 32 columns, halving shared-prefix reads while retaining two recurrence iterations and exact term order. Build, kernelguard, and all 39 validations pass. Dense n1024 improves from the 16-column chunk's 40881.002 to 40764.022 us but remains above the selected 39102.805 us; full geomean is 30039.197 us. CUDA metadata returns to 128 registers/thread for all factor specializations, so this geometry gives up the register reduction while retaining shared-prefix overhead.

Bracketed the less-unrolled in-kernel recurrence at 8-column register chunks. The async eight-warp specialization uses 64 registers/thread versus 80 at chunk 16 and 128 at chunk 32/original 64, with zero local spill; term order and all guards remain unchanged. Build, kernelguard, and all 39 validations pass. Dense n1024 is 41485.985 us and full geomean 30075.930, versus 40881.002/30031.753 at chunk 16, 40764.022/30039.197 at chunk 32, and selected 39102.805/29954.741. Nsys measures total factor time at 3.814 ms versus 3.182 ms at chunk 16 and 1.413 ms selected.

Reworked the admissible fused projected/apply kernel so each six-warp block owns three 16-column output tiles. Every staged V/factor tile feeds all 48 columns, while 70.5 KiB dynamic shared memory permits three resident blocks per SM (18 resident warps at the shared limit) instead of the earlier eight-warp 48-column layout's two blocks. No intermediate projected tensor, concatenation, side scheduling, or events are used. Build, kernelguard, and all 39 validations pass. Dense n1024 is 48557.025 us and full geomean 30431.906, improving the prior eight-warp 48-column result 49474.838/30553.789 but remaining above the prior 32-column fused 47345.889 and selected library 39102.805. Nsys measures four fused launches at 10.369 ms total; the kernel uses 64 registers/thread without local spill.

Narrowed the six-warp fused apply group to two 16-column output tiles. Dynamic shared memory falls from 70.5 to 48 KiB and the kernel uses 56 registers/thread without spill, allowing four shared-limited blocks per SM, but the six-warp geometry requires three projected-row rounds and more 32-column blocks. Build, kernelguard, and all 39 validations pass. Dense n1024 is 50579.061 us and full geomean 30545.521, versus 48557.025/30431.906 for six-warp 48 columns and the earlier eight-warp 32-column 47345.889/30472.095.

Widened the six-warp fused apply group to four 16-column output tiles so each V/factor stage feeds 64 columns. The kernel uses 80 registers/thread and 93 KiB dynamic shared memory, limiting residency to two blocks (12 warps) per SM. Build, kernelguard, and all 39 validations pass. Dense n1024 is 53259.680 us and full geomean 30660.733, versus 48557.025/30431.906 at 48 columns and 50579.061/30545.521 at 32 columns; the 32/48/64 six-warp bracket identifies the 48-column, three-block geometry as the lowest measured target latency.

Restored the measured six-warp, 48-column multi-output fused apply candidate after bracketing 32 and 64 columns. Fresh build, kernelguard, and all 39 validations pass; the repeat is 30460.218 us overall and 48576.129 us dense n1024 versus the first 30431.906/48557.025 and selected library 29954.741/39102.805. Final nsys measures four fused launches at 10.373 ms. Focused NCU confirms 64 registers/thread, no local/shared spill, 72.19 KiB dynamic shared memory, a three-block shared-memory limit, 28.12% theoretical and 26.56-27.46% achieved occupancy, plus 2.0-way average shared-load conflicts.

Continuation trials 38-44 measured both requested refinements from the selected source lineage. For the in-kernel triangular recurrence, 8/16/32-column register chunks retained exact FMA term order and kept completed chunks in the existing shared product tile without a new kernel or global phase. All variants passed kernelguard and all 39 validations. Async factor register counts were 64/80/128 versus 128 for the selected fully unrolled 64-column recurrence, with no local spill; dense n1024 was 41485.985/40881.002/40764.022 versus selected 39102.805 us. Nsys factor totals were 3.814 ms at chunk 8, 3.182 ms at chunk 16, and 1.413 ms selected, measuring the shared-prefix cost of the lower-register variants. For projected/apply reuse, a six-warp kernel staged each V/factor tile once across 2/3/4 output tiles (32/48/64 columns) with 48/70.5/93 KiB dynamic shared memory. Dense n1024 measured 50579.061/48557.025/53259.680 us and overall 30545.521/30431.906/30660.733; the 48-column geometry improved the prior eight-warp 48-column target from 49474.838 to 48557.025 by allowing three resident blocks. Final SHA b6842312f restores that measured 48-column candidate and repeats at 48576.129 us dense, 30460.218 overall. Final nsys reports 10.373 ms across four fused launches. Focused NCU confirms 64 registers/thread, 72.19 KiB dynamic shared, three blocks per SM, 28.12% theoretical and 26.56-27.46% achieved occupancy, no spills, and 2.0-way shared-load conflicts. Fresh build, kernelguard, and all 39 validations pass; worktree source remains on the measured candidate rather than reverting to the selected parent. Profiles for trials 38, 40, 41, and final 44 are under profiles/2026-07-03-13-39-25/.
